verdict: OK to lend in Vapi paper — but only to converters and packaging units with verified cash flows; avoid micro-cap paper mills with nil revenue and stressed working capital.
title: Vapi Paper & Paper Products: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Paper in Vapi is a conversion and packaging trade before it is a mill trade: waste paper and pulp go in, kraft, board and writing-printing paper come out, and cash comes back only after the mill sells to traders and converters. **Value sits in the machine and the power contract, not in the product** — realisations are set by the market and cheaper imports, so a unit's margin is its pulp yield, steam consumption and energy cost. Peer Kuantum cut steam from 1.8 to 0.8 metric tons per ton of pulp and lifted pulp yield 1% through a digester change [4]; that is where the money is made. **The working-capital cycle is the real credit risk**: one rated peer pays suppliers in advance while recovering from customers in 45-60 days, funding the gap with bank WC limits [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the advance-to-supplier percentage and debtor days together; if advances exceed 30 days of purchases, ask how the gap is funded without stretching the limit.

## What has changed now
India-wide paper output (NIC 17) is -0.1% YoY [D], while Gujarat GST collections are running +11.9% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D] — **the state is collecting faster than the country while the paper line itself is flat**. Peer results split: Pudumjee's Q4 FY26 net profit was ₹20 crore on revenue of ₹201 crore, up from ₹190 crore [5], and Kuantum posted 46% QoQ PAT growth to ₹14 crore with EBITDA up 22% to ₹48 crore [6] — but ICRA flags significant capacity addition in the last two years and volatile realisations hit by cheaper imports [11]. **Local Vapi news is thin and partly stale**: a February 2026 report describes Vapi Enterprise as a micro-cap paper company with zero revenue generation [1], and the Moneycontrol Vapi Paper tag carries only 2023 sales figures of ₹0.15 crore and ₹0.69 crore [3] — treat that tag as old. Industrialists' Budget hopes [2] are sentiment, not data.

## Where to grow
**Pursue converters and packaging units feeding Gujarat's industrial belt, not standalone micro mills.** The GST gap [D] says local demand is being invoiced; lend to units with a named buyer list and monthly GST returns matching sales. Avoid zero-revenue shells like the one described in [1] and any borrower whose sales trail the ₹0.15-0.69 crore range in [3] without a clear restart plan.

Take stock statements and debtor ageing every month, GST 2A/2B reconciliation quarterly, and energy bills monthly — power is the swing cost. Where wastewater treatment is involved, obtain the consent-to-operate renewal date upfront; ICRA notes treatment failure can trigger penalties and prolonged shutdown [10].

## Early-warning signs
- **Debtor days crossing 60** (the top of the peer range [8]) for two months -> freeze further drawings and ask for buyer-wise ageing. - **Advance payments to suppliers rising while sales fall** -> reprice or reduce limit. - **Realisations slipping against input cost** [11] -> shift to secured, shorter-tenor facilities. - **Consent-to-operate lapse or pollution notice** [10] -> stop fresh disbursement until renewal is produced.
watch: Debtor days above 60 for two months -> freeze drawings, seek buyer-wise ageing
GST turnover below sanctioned projections by 20% -> reprice limit
Power cost per ton rising with flat sales -> review unit economics
Lapse or notice -> halt fresh disbursement until renewal
Supplier advances beyond 30 days of purchases -> ask funding source
